title: Ministry of Rural Development Participates in World Water Week 2026 in Stockholm
subtitle: India Showcases Community-led Water Security and Rural Development Initiatives at Global Forum
body_text:
The Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India, participated in the World Water Week 2026 being held in Stockholm, Sweden, reaffirming India's commitment to strengthening water security through community-led rural development, technology-enabled governance and sustainable management of natural resources. The global forum provided an important platform for sharing India’s experiences and learning from international best practices in advancing climate-resilient and inclusive water management.
World Water Week, organized by the Stockholm International Water Institute (SIWI), is one of the world’s leading platforms for dialogue, collaboration and innovation on water. The annual event brings together governments, development partners, research institutions and practitioners from across the globe to deliberate on emerging water challenges and share knowledge, experiences and solutions.
Representing the Ministry of Rural Development, Ms. Rohini R. Bhajibhakre, Joint Secretary, participated in the session titled “National Initiative on Water Security: Translating National Water Visions to Reality: What Works?” and shared India’s experience in translating its long-term water vision into institutional and operational approaches for strengthening water security at the grassroots level. The session was convened by Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH and the International Water Management Institute (IWMI).
Highlighting India’s approach, Ms. Bhajibhakre stated that under the visionary leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, water security has emerged as a key pillar of India’s development journey. India’s Water Vision @2047, aligned with the broader vision of Viksit Bharat @2047, seeks to ensure resilient, inclusive and sustainable water security for all citizens through integrated planning, technological innovation and community participation. Water is increasingly being viewed as a foundation for rural prosperity, public health, women’s empowerment, climate resilience and sustainable development.
The Ministry highlighted that India’s water security framework is being advanced through a combination of flagship initiatives, including the Jal Jeevan Mission and the National Initiative on Water Security (NIWS). While Jal Jeevan Mission is strengthening access to safe drinking water in rural areas, NIWS is reinforcing investments in water conservation, groundwater recharge, water harvesting and other water security-related assets through scientific and data-driven planning.
A key element of India’s approach presented at the forum was the National Initiative on Water Security (NIWS), which prioritizes expenditure on water-related works based on groundwater conditions across blocks. This approach provides a clear framework for directing investments towards water-stressed regions and strengthening long-term water security outcomes through objective and transparent planning mechanisms.
The Ministry further highlighted that the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin): VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 places water security among the key focus areas of rural development interventions. The framework promotes convergence between employment generation, livelihood enhancement, natural resource management and creation of durable community assets through participatory planning and implementation.
Technology and Data-driven Planning for Water Security
The Ministry showcased India’s growing use of digital public infrastructure, geospatial technologies and data-driven decision-making for strengthening water security outcomes. Advanced tools such as Yuktdhara - Geospatial Planning Platform, which leverages GIS and remote sensing technologies, support evidence-based planning of rural development and natural resource management interventions. The E-Jal Application facilitates data-driven water budgeting at the Gram Panchayat level by integrating information on water resources, rainfall, groundwater and population.
Capacity building and knowledge dissemination are being strengthened through the E-Saksham Learning Platform, while digital dashboards such as VBGRAMG Soft, SECURE and BhuGRAM enable real-time implementation tracking, financial management, monitoring and transparency across rural development programmes. These technology-enabled systems are helping strengthen decentralized planning and improve the effectiveness of water security interventions across rural India.
The Ministry also emphasized the importance of empowering Gram Panchayats, Village Water and Sanitation Committees and local communities in planning, implementation, operation and maintenance of water-related infrastructure. Community participation, social accountability mechanisms and digital monitoring systems have emerged as important pillars for ensuring transparency, sustainability and long-term impact of rural water investments.
On 25 August 2026, Ms. Bhajibhakre also participated in the High-Level Panel titled “Financing Water Resilience and Prosperity: Translating Commitments into Implementation and Sustainable Impact ahead of the UN 2026 Water Conference.” The session brought together ministers, multilateral development banks, climate finance institutions and development partners to discuss approaches for strengthening investments in water resilience and achieving Sustainable Development Goal.
During the discussion, India highlighted the importance of strong political commitment, cooperative federalism, robust digital public infrastructure and community-centered planning in ensuring that investments in water security translate into sustainable outcomes for citizens and communities.
India’s participation in World Water Week 2026 reflects the Ministry of Rural Development’s continued commitment to advancing water security as an integral component of rural development, livelihoods, climate resilience and sustainable management of natural resources. The participation also contributed to the global dialogue on strengthening water security through local planning, technology-enabled governance and community-led action.
About World Water Week
Organized annually by the Stockholm International Water Institute (SIWI), World Water Week is a leading global platform for dialogue, collaboration and innovation on water. It brings together governments, development partners, researchers, practitioners and other stakeholders from around the world to advance knowledge, partnerships and solutions for addressing global water challenges.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Rural Development participated in World Water Week 2026 in Stockholm, where Joint Secretary Rohini R. Bhajibhakre showcased India's community-led water security initiatives, including the Jal Jeevan Mission, the National Initiative on Water Security (NIWS), and digital tools like Yuktdhara and E-Jal. She also spoke at a high-level panel on financing water resilience ahead of the UN 2026 Water Conference. The event served as a platform for India to share its water governance experiences and learn from global best practices.
enrichment.context: World Water Week, organized by the Stockholm International Water Institute (SIWI), is an annual global gathering on water policy and innovation. India's participation reflects its ongoing efforts to position water security as central to rural development, citing schemes such as the Jal Jeevan Mission for drinking water access and the newer National Initiative on Water Security, which prioritizes investment based on groundwater stress data. The release also references the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025, which integrates water security into rural employment and livelihood programmes, alongside digital governance tools like Yuktdhara (geospatial planning) and E-Jal (Gram Panchayat-level water budgeting). This release is essentially a report of India's participation and advocacy at an international forum, reiterating existing schemes and digital infrastructure rather than announcing new policy.
